test_title: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 12 Aug, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: In Indian State governments, to whom is the State Council of Ministers collectively responsible?

options.text: Chief Justice of the concerned State

solution:
The Correct answer is __**State Legislative Assembly**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **State Council of Ministers** in India is collectively responsible to the **State Legislative Assembly**, as per Article 164 of the **Indian Constitution**.
 
• The **State Legislative Assembly**, also called the **Vidhan Sabha**, is the lower house of the state legislature in states with a bicameral legislature or the sole legislative body in states with a unicameral legislature.
 
• This principle of collective responsibility ensures that the council acts as a single entity and is accountable to the legislature for its policies and decisions.
 
• If the Legislative Assembly passes a vote of no confidence against the Council of Ministers, they are bound to resign collectively, including the Chief Minister.
 
• The **Chief Minister**, as the head of the Council of Ministers, plays a key role in ensuring the accountability of the council to the Legislative Assembly.
 
• This system is a fundamental aspect of the **parliamentary system of government** in India and is modeled on the British parliamentary system.
 
• The Legislative Assembly comprises elected representatives of the people, making it the most appropriate body for ensuring the accountability of the executive branch to the citizens.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Governor of the State**__

 __
 
• The **Governor** is the constitutional head of the state and acts on the advice of the Council of Ministers headed by the Chief Minister.
 
• While the Governor appoints the Chief Minister and other ministers, the Council of Ministers is not collectively responsible to the Governor.
 
• The Governor has certain discretionary powers, but the executive powers of the state are exercised by the Council of Ministers.
 
 
 
• **Council of States**__
 __
 
• The **Council of States**, commonly referred to as the **Rajya Sabha**, is the upper house of the Indian Parliament and does not play a direct role in the functioning of state governments.
 
• It represents the interests of the states at the national level and primarily deals with matters concerning the Union and its territories.
 
 
 
• **Chief Justice of the concerned State**__
 
 
• The **Chief Justice of the High Court** is the head of the judiciary in a state and ensures justice under the legal framework.
 
• The judiciary functions independently of the executive and legislature and does not have a role in the accountability of the Council of Ministers.
